description: Folder that holds instances, backups and panel data.
Docker image of Odoo; the tag is the Odoo version.
Versions offered: "auto" (every published version of the official image from odoo_min_version) or a comma-separated list such as 17.0,18.0,saas-18.2.
Oldest version offered when odoo_versions is "auto".

Download the Odoo image of every offered version, and the PostgreSQL image, in the background, so the first instance of a version does not wait for the download (each Odoo image takes 1-3 GB of disk).
Docker image of each instance's database.
Password of the Odoo user "admin" in new instances.
Memory one instance's Odoo container may use, in Docker units (512m, 2g); 0: no limit.
Memory one instance's database container may use, in Docker units (512m, 1g); 0: no limit.
Processor cores one instance's Odoo may use; 0: no limit.
Processor cores one instance's database may use; 0: no limit.
Processes and threads one instance container may run at the same time.
Size of a container log file before it is rotated (10m).
Rotated log files kept per container.

What happens when an instance's containers or files were changed outside the panel: "warn" (report it) or "restore" (report it, then recreate Odoo and its database from the panel's own configuration). Connectors are only ever reported.
Where Enterprise add-ons come from: "folder", "git" or "none".
folder source: where the add-ons of a version are; {version} (19.0) and {major} (19) are replaced.
git source: repository holding one branch per Odoo version.
git source: branch name of a version, e.g. {version}.
Module whose presence proves the add-ons are there.
How instances are reached: "cloudflare-quick" or "host-ports".
cloudflare-quick: connector image.
cloudflare-quick: container name prefix.
cloudflare-quick: first status port of a connector.
cloudflare-quick: status port of the panel connector.
host-ports: the server's public name or address.
host-ports: scheme of the public addresses.
What starts code updates, comma-separated: "polling", "github-app" (the GitHub App's webhook), "github-webhook" (one webhook per repository).
github-webhook: the secret entered on GitHub (20 or more random characters).
Where the panel keeps its own data: "sqlite".
How user names and passwords are checked: "local" (the panel's accounts).
Second factors offered at sign-in, comma-separated: "email", "totp" or both.
Who must use a second factor: "none", "admins" or "everyone".
How the panel sends e-mail: "smtp" or "none".
Sender of the panel's e-mails, e.g. Sudoo.sh <no-reply@example.com>.
smtp: the mail server; empty: no e-mail (and no e-mail codes).
smtp: port (587 for STARTTLS, 465 for SSL).
smtp: encryption.
smtp: user name, usually the full e-mail address.
smtp: password or app password.
Folder with a layout.html that replaces the built-in frame of every e-mail.
Hours an invitation link works before it expires (it works once).
When administrators may set a new account's password instead of inviting the person by e-mail: "no_mail" (only while e-mail is not set up), "always" or "never".
Invitations one administrator may send (new or again) per hour.
Recovery codes made for an account that uses an authenticator app.
E-mail people each time their account signs in (when e-mail is set up).
People may turn the sign-in e-mail off for their own account.
Accent colour of e-mails, as #RRGGBB.
Language of the web app for accounts that have not chosen one: "en" or "ar".
Where request counts are kept: "memory".
Requests that read, per minute, per signed-in user or address; 0: no limit.
Requests that change something, per minute, per user or address; 0: no limit.
Instances on this server at most; 0: no limit.
Instances one user (or API token) may own; 0: no limit.
Minutes a user must wait between two creations; 0: no wait.
Memory kept free for the operating system and Docker, in MB (the larger of this and capacity_reserve_percent is used).
Memory kept free for the operating system and Docker, in % of the server's.
Memory one running instance is counted with while none has been measured yet, in MB.
Server memory use, in %, from which the dashboard warns that instances may slow down.
Instances running at once at most: creating or starting one more is refused; 0: never refused, only warned.

Where the gateways run: "service" (their own container, sudoo-gateway: instances keep answering while the panel restarts; the panel serves them itself while that container is not running) or "embedded" (inside the panel process, as before 3.0).
service mode: seconds the gateway service may not answer the panel before the panel serves the instances itself (at once when the service stopped normally).
Largest request body a visitor may send to an instance (uploads, imports), in MB.
Seconds a visitor may send nothing while sending a request body before the gateway gives up.
Largest single WebSocket message passed to or from an instance, in MB.
Seconds a visitor's connection has to send a request's headers (and is kept open while idle).
Visitors' connections open at once to one instance's gateway; more are answered 503.
Visitors' connections open at once to all gateways together; more are answered 503.

Custom domains for instances: "off", "acme" (the gateway answers on ports 80 and 443 and gets a certificate for each domain from an ACME authority such as Let's Encrypt) or "external" (something in front, such as your own Cloudflare tunnel or proxy, handles https; the panel only records the domains).
The ACME authority: "production" (Let's Encrypt), "staging" (Let's Encrypt's test authority: certificates browsers do not trust, for trying things out) or the https address of another ACME directory.
Contact e-mail given to the ACME authority; empty: ADMIN_CONTACT_EMAIL, or none.
Renew a certificate this many days before it expires.
Longest wait between two attempts after a certificate could not be issued.
Custom domains one instance may have; 0: none.
The name (or address) custom domains point to; empty: PUBLIC_HOST. A name is shown as a CNAME record, an address as an A or AAAA record.
Seconds a DNS lookup of a custom domain may take.
Before asking for a certificate, check that the domain reaches this server over http (port 80), as the ACME authority will.
Port the gateway answers custom domains on over http.
Port the gateway answers custom domains on over https.
Port of the panel: the web service (sudoo-web) listens here.
Port of the backend (127.0.0.1 only); the web service forwards to it.
Port of the live event stream (127.0.0.1 only).
First gateway port (one per instance).
First Odoo port (one per instance, 127.0.0.1 only).
Pause an instance after this many hours without visits; 0: never.
New instances pause when idle (each instance can change it).
New instances get new code automatically.
New instances upgrade changed modules after an update.
Lifetime offered for new instances, in days; 0: keep.
Instances that may be in the production stage at the same time; 0: no limit.
New production instances get new code automatically (off: updates only when someone asks, or once switched on for the instance).
Lifetime offered for new staging instances, in days; 0: keep.
Staging instances get the daily backup too (when daily_backups is on).
polling: check GitHub for new commits this often.
Panel sign-out after this long without activity.
Longest panel session.
Who users are told to contact.
Seconds between two measurements of the server and the instances.
Back up every instance that was used since its last daily backup, once a day; each keeps only its latest daily backup.
When the daily backups run (HH:MM, 24 hours).
Time zone of the daily backup time, for example Africa/Cairo.
How long the state before a restore is kept, and Rollback offered, after a restore (hours).
Back up an instance before an update changes its code, and put it back (code, and the database when it may have changed) when the update fails.
Copy backups to S3-compatible storage off this server (Cloudflare R2, AWS S3, Backblaze B2, MinIO...), each copy with a manifest of SHA-256 checksums signed with the panel's Ed25519 key.
Address of the storage's S3 API, e.g. https://<account>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com or https://s3.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com (https; http only for localhost).
Region of the bucket ("auto" for Cloudflare R2; us-east-1, eu-central-1, ... otherwise).
The bucket the copies go to (create it first; keep it private).
Folder inside the bucket for this panel's copies (several panels can share a bucket).
How the bucket is addressed: "path" (endpoint/bucket/file: R2, MinIO, B2, S3) or "virtual" (bucket.endpoint/file).
Access key ID of a key that may read and write the bucket.
The secret of that access key (stored encrypted).
Copy the backups of staging and development instances off-site too (production instances' backups are always copied while off-site copies are on).
Which backups are copied, comma-separated: manual, daily, deletion, before-update, before-restore, before-rollback, before-repair.
Production: keep the newest copy of each of this many most recent days.
Production: keep the newest copy of each of this many most recent months too.
Staging and development: keep the newest copy of each of this many days.
Staging and development: keep the newest copy of each of this many months too.
Download and check the newest copy of each instance again when none was verified for this many days (signature and every checksum); 0: only when someone asks.
Seconds one request to the storage may wait for an answer.
Tell people when something needs attention (a failed job, an instance down, a full disk), by e-mail and webhooks; off: no alert is sent or listed.
Send alert e-mails to every super admin with an address.
More addresses that receive alert e-mails, comma-separated (an on-call mailbox, say).
Alert when a job fails (with its plain hint and a link).
Alert when an update failed and was rolled back, or its rollback failed too.
Alert when a backup fails (manual, daily or before a change).
Alert when an instance that should run does not answer for alert_instance_down_minutes.
Minutes an instance must stay down before the alert.
Alert when the free disk falls below alert_disk_free_percent.
Free disk, in % of the disk holding ODOO_ROOT, below which the alert is sent.
Alert when server memory stays above capacity_warning_percent for alert_memory_minutes.
Minutes memory must stay above the warning before the alert.
Alert when an instance was changed outside the panel (drift).
Alert when a backup could not be copied off-site, or a copy failed its check.
Alert when a production instance has had no successful off-site copy for alert_offsite_missing_hours (while off-site copies are on).
Hours without a successful off-site copy of a production instance before the alert.
Alert when the panel or a running instance has no public link for alert_public_link_minutes.
Minutes without a public link before the alert.
Alert when a custom domain's certificate cannot be issued or renewed, or expires within alert_certificate_days.
Days before a certificate expires from which it is shown and alerted as expiring.
Send a notice when a problem that was alerted is over (back online, disk freed).
The same alert is sent at most once in this many minutes; 0: every time.
E-mail one summary a day instead of each alert as it happens (webhooks and the bell still get each alert at once).
When the daily summary is sent (HH:MM, TIMEZONE).
Seconds a webhook may take to answer before the delivery counts as failed.
Webhook 1: address alerts are posted to (https).
Webhook 1: key of the X-Sudoo-Signature HMAC-SHA256.
Webhook 1: "json" (signed JSON), "slack", "discord" or "teams" (incoming webhooks).
Webhook 2: address alerts are posted to (https).
Webhook 2: key of the X-Sudoo-Signature HMAC-SHA256.
Webhook 2: "json", "slack", "discord" or "teams".
Webhook 3: address alerts are posted to (https).
Webhook 3: key of the X-Sudoo-Signature HMAC-SHA256.
Webhook 3: "json", "slack", "discord" or "teams".
People whose role allows it can open a terminal in an instance's containers from the panel (the Shell tab); off: nobody can, and open shells close.

Who may open a shell in an instance's Odoo container: "admins" (super admins and administrators), "maintainers" (and maintainers) or "developers" (and developers). Viewers never can; psql in the database container stays with super admins and administrators.
Shells in production instances: "off" (nobody), "super_admins" (super admins only) or "allowed" (whoever may open shells in other instances). Each one is confirmed when it is opened.
Super admins may open the Odoo container's shell as root (the container's capabilities stay dropped); off: every shell runs as the container's own user.
A shell nobody types in for this long closes.
Longest a shell stays open; it then closes (a new one can be opened).
Shells one person may have open at the same time.
Shells open in one instance at the same time.
Seconds the one-time ticket that connects a new shell stays valid.
Record what is typed and shown in shells: "off", "production" (shells in production instances and root shells) or "all". Recordings are encrypted; only super admins can play them.
Days recordings, and the list of past shells, are kept.
Largest recording of one shell, in MB; beyond it only what is typed is recorded, and the shell closes when that alone reaches the size again.
Space all shell recordings may take together, in MB; the oldest go first.
Use the Sudoo.sh marketplace: register with the hub, send a signed heartbeat every 15 minutes, install plugins. Off: the panel never contacts the hub; installed free plugins keep working.
Address of the Sudoo.sh hub (https; http only for localhost while testing).
The hub's root public keys (Ed25519, base64url, comma-separated); empty: the keys this release ships for hub.sudoo.sh, or the hub's keys as first seen for another hub.
